sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Chrome DevTools MCP lets an AI coding agent such as Claude, Cursor, Copilot or Antigravity control and inspect a live Chrome browser. It works as an MCP server or a command-line tool and gives the agent DevTools features: performance traces, network requests, screenshots and console messages.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents usually can't see what their web code does in a real browser. This tool lets them open pages, click through them, record performance traces and read console errors, so they can debug and verify front-end work themselves.
whoFor: Web developers using AI coding agents
Teams automating browser checks with agents
Anyone who wants an agent to test pages in Chrome
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for official Chrome DevTools features in your agent, from the Chrome DevTools team. It officially supports Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only.
requirements: An MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and others)

overview: You add one entry to your MCP client's config that runs npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest. When the agent uses a tool that needs a browser, the server starts Chrome automatically. It uses Puppeteer to automate actions and wait for their results, and Chrome DevTools to record traces and extract performance insights.

The same package includes a chrome-devtools CLI for controlling the browser from a terminal without MCP, and a set of skills that teach agents to debug accessibility, cookies, Largest Contentful Paint and memory leaks. Claude Code, Copilot in VS Code and Gemini CLI can install everything as a plugin.

Be aware of the disclaimers: the server exposes the browser's content to your MCP client, so avoid using it with sensitive data. Google collects usage statistics by default (opt out with --no-usage-statistics), and performance tools may send trace URLs to the CrUX API (disable with --no-performance-crux).

steps.title: Add the server to your MCP client
steps.body: See the Client Configurations Guide for your editor or agent.

steps.title: Open a page and take a screenshot
steps.code:
chrome-devtools navigate_page 1 --url "https://developers.chrome.com"
chrome-devtools take_screenshot 1 --filePath screenshot.png
chrome-devtools stop
